subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I should build the full module economically but solidly, sticking to only the API methods I'm confident exist like createBuilder, joint, chain, sweep, part, loft, and the various geometry primitives, to avoid relying on anything unverifiable.

Planning the scene concretely: a red panda standing on all fours atop a small stone, facing forward. I'm sketching coordinates for the stone (radius 0.3, height 0.14) and the panda's body, legs, spine, neck, head, tail, and facial features, mapping each part to joints and bones so the skeleton drives the body, head, muzzle, nose, jaw, and eyes placement in world space.

Now I'm working out the eyes, ears, cheek ruffs, and tear-mark details using small spheres, cones, and capsules in cream, rust, and dark tones, then turning to the legs — figuring out how the limb-to-chain helper functions map lengths, points, and names so each leg sweep gets the right number of segments and radii for the dark brown fur.

I'm placing front and hind leg roots and targets relative to the stone perch, checking reach distances against bone lengths, and deciding bend directions per limb before attaching paw spheres at the chain tip. Then I'm plotting the tail as a curved spline of points sweeping back and down to rest against the stone's curvature.

Actually the tail was hanging in open air, so I'm curving it upward instead into a balanced, raised, curled shape with tapering radius along the sweep, then painting alternating rust bands with a dark tip. For the stone I'm considering an icosahedron-based form with a mossy grey paint treatment.

I need to give the stone its own joint since nothing else sits near the origin, so I'm adding a dedicated "stone" joint and reparenting hips to it. The stone itself becomes a flat cylinder with scattered green moss spheres fused on top to simulate patchy lichen.

I'm adding a small glowing cyan crystal accent on the stone for a bit of visual flair, plus setting up a cel-shaded paint helper so the coat reads rust-toned on lit areas and darker on shadowed/belly regions, with an eye plane planned for the head.

Now I'm figuring out eye placement—using an SVG texture on a plane oriented toward the front, with dark ellipse base, white highlight, and amber iris, positioned carefully against the head sphere's curved surface so it sits flush rather than buried inside the geometry.

I'm writing a helper function that projects a direction vector onto the ellipsoid surface to compute exact eye placement, then adding a small normal offset so the eye sits just outside the skin. Since I'm using world coordinates where +X is left, I'll keep things symmetric and just label the side as L for clarity, then move on to shaping cream-colored cone ruffs along the cheeks.

Now I'm defining the ears as flattened spheres with inner cream discs, placing a belly stripe and dark chest patch using the surface normal's Y value to decide where dark fur goes, skipping whiskers but adding a cream muzzle patch, and setting up moss-like noise coloring on the stone texture where the surface faces upward.

For the tail, I'm using a sine function along the segment index to create alternating ring colors. I'm also setting up the skeletal structure: a jaw joint aimed from the head with upper and lower jaw spheres (cream lower jaw, darker mouth interior), a head joint parented to the neck, and a neck-to-chest joint chain to complete the spine.
